# Persona Vectors: Monitoring and Controlling Character Traits in Language Models

**Link:** https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.21509  ·  **Code/Data:** https://github.com/safety-research/persona_vectors
**Authors:** Runjin Chen, Andy Arditi, Henry Sleight, Owain Evans, Jack Lindsey  ·  **Venue/Date:** arXiv Jul 2025 (v3 Sep 2025); ICLR 2026

## Gist
- Character traits of the Assistant (evil, sycophancy, hallucination, plus optimistic/impolite/apathetic/humorous) correspond to linear **persona vectors** in the residual stream, extractable fully automatically from a natural-language trait description.
- The same vector serves three jobs: **monitor** trait expression at inference (prompt-induced shifts), **predict/explain** trait shifts caused by finetuning (shift of activations along the vector correlates r = 0.76–0.97 with trait change), and **control** (inference-time inhibition, or "preventative steering" during training).
- Projection of *training data* onto the vector flags samples that will induce the trait, including ones an LLM filter misses — a data-hygiene tool directly tied to emergent-misalignment-style generalisation.

## Setup & technical details
- Models: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct.
- Pipeline artefacts per trait (generated by a frontier model from the trait description): 5 contrastive system-prompt pairs (pos/neg), 40 questions (20 extraction / 20 held-out eval), and a scoring rubric; GPT-4.1-mini judges trait expression 0–100 and coherence.
- Finetuning datasets: explicit trait-eliciting sets (evil, sycophancy, hallucination) and "EM-like" narrow sets (Medical, Code, GSM8K, Math, Opinions) each in Normal / Mistake-I (mild) / Mistake-II (overt) variants, modelled on Betley et al.'s emergent misalignment setup.
- Real-world test on LMSYS-Chat-1M subsets.
- Capability check: MMLU; coherence judged >80 kept as acceptable.

## Methods / techniques
- **Persona vector (diff-of-means)**: run 10 rollouts per extraction question under pos and neg system prompts; keep responses with trait score >50 (pos) / <50 (neg); take mean residual activation over *response tokens* at every layer; v_ℓ = mean(pos) − mean(neg). Pick the layer by steering effectiveness sweep (Appendix B.4). Reusable recipe; identical to Zhen Hong's diff-of-means directions.
- **Inference-time steering**: h_ℓ ← h_ℓ ± α·v_ℓ at all response positions. Subtracting inhibits the trait; large α costs MMLU.
- **Monitoring by projection**: project the activation at the *last prompt token* onto v_ℓ; predicts trait score of the yet-to-be-generated response.
- **Finetuning shift**: Δ = mean projection of finetuned-model activations − base-model activations on a fixed prompt set; correlate with trait-score change.
- **Preventative steering**: during finetuning add +α·v_ℓ to activations so the model need not shift its weights to express the trait the data pushes for; then deploy without steering. Multi-layer version approaches baseline trait levels with no MMLU loss.
- **Projection difference for data flagging**: for each training sample, projection of its response onto v minus projection of the base model's own response to the same prompt; aggregate per dataset or rank per sample.

## Key results
- Prompt-induced monitoring: last-token projection vs subsequent trait score r = 0.75–0.83 (system-prompt and many-shot variants).
- Finetuning: shift along the matching persona vector vs trait expression r = 0.76–0.97, above cross-trait baselines (r = 0.34–0.86) — the vector is trait-specific, not a generic "finetuned-ness" axis.
- Narrow mistake datasets induce broad trait shifts, e.g. flawed math reasoning raises evil; Mistake-II variants shift more than Mistake-I.
- Post-hoc inhibition works but degrades MMLU at high α; preventative steering keeps coherence >80 average and preserves MMLU better.
- Dataset-level projection difference strongly predicts post-finetune trait expression; sample-level projections separate trait-inducing from control samples cleanly.
- LMSYS: high-projection samples induce the strongest shifts; after an LLM-based filter removes explicit examples, the method still finds residual inducers (toxic requests → evil, romantic role-play → sycophancy, under-specified queries → hallucination).

## Insights & takeaways
- Traits that post-training tries to suppress are still linearly present and manipulable; finetuning tends to move the model *along pre-existing directions* rather than build new ones — consistent with the Persona Selection Model.
- A single direction supports both read-out and write-in, i.e. here "decodable" and "causal" coincide — but the paper selects the layer *by causal steering*, which is why; probes alone would not guarantee this.
- "Emergent misalignment" becomes measurable as a geometric displacement before any behavioural eval is run.

## Relevance to my research
- **Project B**: the retention-vs-release direction is a persona vector in all but name; adopt their last-prompt-token projection as an online monitor at goodbye turns, and their projection-difference score to audit companion-chat finetuning data.
- **Project C**: use preventative steering as a control — if adding the "dismissive" persona vector during LoRA training on tracer stories changes tracer uptake, that is causal evidence for "persona gates expression" beyond system prompts.
- **Project A**: compute an "evil/hostile" vector on Qwen3-8B and test whether the grudge penalty's activation-patching signal is aligned with it (rival explanation: generic hostility vs targeted retrieval).
- **Methodology**: cross-trait correlation baseline (r = 0.34–0.86) is the right specificity control for any claimed direction; replicate on Qwen3-8B and Gemma 4 12B rather than assume transfer.
- Open gap the lane can fill: all evals are single-turn; multi-turn drift of the projection is exactly Projects A/B/D.

## Caveats & critiques
- Only two 7–8B models; three main traits; one LLM judge; single-turn.
- Supervised: needs a trait you can already elicit by system prompt; cannot find unknown traits.
- Finetuning-shift correlations are across datasets, not within-sample causal evidence that the direction *mediates* the behaviour.
- Projection difference requires generating base-model responses for every sample (cost); approximations in appendix.
- Exact layers per model/trait are only in appendix figures, not stated in text.

## Related
- [[The Persona Selection Model]] — cites this as evidence that traits are reused pre-training representations.
- [[The Assistant Axis - Situating and Stabilizing the Default Persona of Language Models]] — same group; moves from single traits to the dominant axis of persona space.
- [[What Models Express, Suppress, and Resist - Auditing Open-Weight LLMs with Persona Vectors]] — scales this pipeline to 53 traits on Qwen3-8B / gpt-oss-20b.
- [[Refusal Lives Downstream of Persona in Chat Models]] — uses the same extraction recipe to show persona vectors gate refusal.
- [[Do LLMs Experience an Internal Polylogue]] — treats persona-vector projections as a time series during reasoning.
